=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clear paired leaves at visible nodes along the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear grouped near the top of the stem, with little internodal space between nodes)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without subdivisions)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (smooth margin with no teeth or serrations visible)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering to both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is gently curved, not tapered or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off on either side)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, moderately spaced, 4-6 pairs per leaf (secondary veins clearly visible, arching from midrib to margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface reflects light, appears glossy)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is relatively short, less than 1/3 the length of the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (round in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears soft and green, not woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green (stem is light green, consistent with young growth)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels visible on the stem surface)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate or milky sap visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base visible; not applicable for Fabaceae unless confirmed)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: The seedling appears to be a young, healthy individual with opposite, simple, elliptic leaves. The leaves are glossy, entire, and arranged in a clustered fashion near the apex. Stem is green and herbaceous. No damage, trichomes, stipules, latex, or tendrils are visible. The presence of an orange tag suggests it may be part of a monitoring or research plot. All images show the same individual from slightly different angles, confirming consistency in morphology.
